analysis.title: Cooler Jobs Data Take Heat Off US Bonds
key_insights: September non-farm payrolls rose 29k, below the 80k expected and well below August's slightly revised 133k.
The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, driven by higher participation. Wage growth was 0.1% MoM.
Job growth was mildly positive across most sectors. Only tech, finance, business services and government recorded negligible declines, which TS Lombard reads as noise.
The US labour market has turned the corner in 2026, but the reacceleration is not fast enough to have the Fed raising rates aggressively.
The Fed hiked in September. An October move was always unlikely, as Fed officials confirmed this week.
The US bond market agrees and some pressure on forward rates has eased.
TS Lombard expects further labour market improvement into 2027, which should keep the Fed on a quarterly hiking path. Terminal rate pricing now looks about right.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Weaker than the 80k expected. Seen as erratic weakness after an erratically strong August, so little change to the Fed outlook.
The consensus figure the print missed.
The strong August reading had agitated rate-hike hawks.
Up from 4.1%, thanks to stronger participation, which is generally a good thing.
Very subdued wage growth, which eases inflation pressure on the Fed.

risk_factors: Labour market reacceleration could continue into 2027 and keep the Fed on a quarterly hiking path.
Payroll data volatility in 2026 is at new extremes, so single prints are unreliable.
geopolitical: France is experiencing a sudden implosion of its bond market.
